title: Elasticity from a demand schedule: price elasticity, the total revenue test and substitutes
scenario: Ridgeway Pottery, an invented studio, sells handmade mugs. The table shows the number of mugs buyers demand per month at four prices.

stimulus.title: Demand for Ridgeway mugs
stimulus.html:
Mugs demanded per month at each price (invented data for practice)
PriceQuantity demanded
$10100
$8150
$6180
$4200

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the price elasticity of demand when the price falls from $10 to $8, using the starting values. Show your work.

rubric.point: Correct percent changes: quantity +50% ((150 − 100) ÷ 100) and price −20% ((8 − 10) ÷ 10)

parts.sample: Percent change in quantity: <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>150</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mn>100</mn></mfrac><mo>×</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{150 - 100}{100} \times 100</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 50\%</annotation></semantics></math>. Percent change in price: <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo>×</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{8 - 10}{10} \times 100 = -20\%</annotation></semantics></math>. Elasticity: <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>÷</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>20</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|50 \div (-20)| = 2.5</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify what happens to Ridgeway's total revenue when the price falls from $10 to $8, and state whether this is consistent with your answer to part A.

rubric.point: Total revenue increases, from $1,000 to $1,200, consistent with elastic demand (elasticity above 1) in this range
accept: rises, as expected with elastic demand

parts.sample: Total revenue increases from <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>$</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10 \times 100 = $1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>150</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>$</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8 \times 150 = $1{,}200</annotation></semantics></math>. This is consistent with part A: an elasticity of 2.5 is greater than 1, so demand is elastic, and with elastic demand price and total revenue move in opposite directions.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Ridgeway considers cutting the price from $6 to $4. Using the total revenue test, explain whether demand is elastic or inelastic in this range.

rubric.point: Inelastic, because total revenue falls ($1,080 to $800) when the price falls: price and total revenue move in the same direction
accept: inelastic since TR falls with the price cut

parts.sample: Total revenue falls from <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>$</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>080</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6 \times 180 = $1{,}080</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="mic-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>200</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>$</mo><mn>800</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 \times 200 = $800</annotation></semantics></math>. Price and total revenue move in the same direction, so demand is inelastic in this range.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: A new studio opens in the same town and sells handmade mugs much like Ridgeway's. Explain how this is likely to affect the price elasticity of demand for Ridgeway's mugs.

rubric.point: Demand becomes more elastic, because buyers now have a close substitute and can switch to it when Ridgeway raises its price

parts.sample: Demand for Ridgeway's mugs becomes more elastic. The new studio's mugs are a close substitute, so if Ridgeway raises its price, more buyers switch to the other studio, and quantity demanded falls by a larger percentage than before.
